result.title: Sequential auditing of connected forecast errors under partial observations
result.summary: Graph forecasting systems often rely on prediction intervals to quantify uncertainty across connected locations, but the true outcomes needed for evaluation may be only partially observed. We study how an auditor can selectively retrieve missing outcomes to determine whether there exists a connected group whose outcomes violate the same side of their respective forecast intervals. The audit stops when the observed labels determine the event or the query budget is exhausted. On three public graph time series, MOMS reduces mean queries by 19.6% to 38.5% relative to screened random acquisition when 30% of labels are hidden. Under localized masking on METR-LA, shortest witness finds more positive cases within ten queries, although the difference depends on node ordering. Direct component traversal reproduces all 9,696 screened random traces without enumerating connected subsets. The experiments show that reducing queries to a decision does not necessarily improve early event discovery or reduce local computation.

AI.brief_summary: 研究部分观测下图时间序列预测区间的序贯审计：审计者选择性查询缺失标签，以判定是否存在连通节点组同侧违反各自预测区间，在观测足以定论或查询预算耗尽时停止，并在三个公开数据上比较查询策略与开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「选择性获取证据—判定即停—预算约束」的框架与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中的证据筛选、停止决策和查询成本问题概念相通，可能为 LVR 的观察预算取舍提供参照，但跨领域可迁移性尚需核查。
